Better than the average two-parter. I liked the buildup, the comic timing, and this face. Still, I must wonder what was going on in the minds of the Mane Six at times, or lack thereof. It was obvious to me at the get-go that bringing back the heroes of yore could also bring back the villain. That would seem a far more likely outcome than tearing a hole in the fabric of spacetime or somesuch, but for all their fretting about what could happen, that never occurs to them! Also, why do none of them suggest enlisting the help of Discord, or at least Celestia and Luna? (I guess that's one solution to the problem I mentioned earlier: Just momentarily forget about Discord entirely.)

There have certainly been a lot of elements introduced to the series in episodes written by M.A. Larson to be expanded upon later — Discord, Tartarus, time travel spells, and now Star Swirl — that seemed at first to be one-time deals. One must wonder about the origins of these concepts: Whether Larson came up with them himself and other writers took the ideas and ran with them later, or he was assigned to introduce them by the powers that be. (As someone who used to work in the industry, I can tell you that individual episodes of TV shows are written by committee a lot more than the credits would have you believe.)

As soon as it was mentioned that the Elements might need to be sacrificed, I knew that would almost certainly not be the case. Perhaps that's because sacrifice doesn't seem to be a theme the series dwells upon too much, as it's deemed inappropriate for the age of the audience, kind of like how nobody actually dies in the Goosebumps books. Or maybe Hasbro would look down at any plot twist that might hurt sales of Elements-related merchandise. That being said, I suppose things might be different in the series finale...

One final thing. As soon as I heard the voice of Star Swirl, I got the feeling I should look up his actor. Seems my instincts proved correct: He got his start in two early Cronenberg movies!
